title: Back Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with fever, chills, unilateral flank pain/CVA tenderness, nausea, vomiting, and lower urinary tract symptoms (dysuria, frequency, urgency). Acute pyelonephritis is an ascending bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma — most commonly E. coli (80%). Risk factors: female, sexual activity, pregnancy, urinary tract obstruction, catheterization, DM, immunosuppression. UA shows pyuria, leukocyte esterase, nitrites, WBC casts. Urine culture for confirmation + sensitivities. Blood cultures if severe/septic. CT abdomen/pelvis if complicated (abscess, obstruction, stone) or not responding to 48-72h of antibiotics. Treatment: outpatient (mild, stable): PO fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin) or TMP-SMX. Inpatient (severe, vomiting, pregnant, immunocompromised): IV ceftriaxone or fluoroquinolone. Switch to PO after clinical improvement. Total course 7-14 days. Repeat urine culture after treatment to confirm clearance.
